answer: Pulse-committed lottery admission assigns each identity a slot through a randomness beacon whose seed stays sealed until after registration closes, so no attacker can precompute favorable outcomes. The kernel of enforcement is that a claim only validates if its commitment lands inside a short window derived from that beacon. Because pre-registering many identities yields no advantage and losers pay the full admission cost, each surviving sybil carries a real per-identity fee. A lotus bloom per round determines how many winners clear, keeping issuance finite.
